text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Albanian opposition parties have protested to foreign embassies over Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi's declaration that his ruling Democrats were ready for a civil war if that was what the Socialists wanted.
- A senior Socialist leader, Sabit Brokaj, put under house arrest for allegedly ordering violent demonstrations, has said President Sali Berisha wanted his arrest at any cost.

- A group of men, saying they were members of the political prisoners association, kicked chairman Kurt Kola out of the group's headquarters saying he had betrayed their ideals by teaming with the leftist opposition against the government.
- The paper publishes what is says are pages from the diary of Shemsie Kadria, the president of the collapsed Gjallica scheme, which say he gave the ruling Democratic Party $100,000.
- Four civilians forced the driver of the Socialist Party secretary general Rexhep Mejdani to take his car to the outskirts of Tirana and threw it down a hill.
- Main opposition parties turn down an invitation for roundtable discussions with the Democrats over the crisis.
- Italy refuses to sign cooperation agreement with Albania before it gets guarantees that free market rules will be observed.
- A group of sympathisers of the ruling Democratic Party in the southern town of Fier attacked a crowd of peaceful demonstrators with sticks, wounding five demonstrators.
- Rightist parties will attend a roundtable with the ruling Democrats only if the resignation of the government is discussed.
- The Forum for Democracy has called for peaceful protests at midday in Tirana's main square, in the western port of Durres and the central town of Elbasan.
- The Socialist Party has hailed a statement by German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel who said the crisis was created because of the licensing of pyramid investment schemes.
- The paper says the Democratic Party is a guarantee for democracy in Albania.
- President Sali Berisha said dialogue had to start with all Albanians who were eager to overcome the problems caused by the collapse of pyramid schemes.
